elements.scope_reason: Four findings with a 'dehydration likely' conclusion.
elements.problem: The four parts (thirst, dry mouth, poor skin turgor, BP < 90/60) are each encoded with a fitting concept, BP < 90/60 correctly as SBP < 90 or DBP < 60, and the conclusion is a probable Dehydration rule referenced by the priority rule. The logic is wrong: the rule uses 'or' across the four, so thirst alone (or dry mouth alone) in a tired patient yields a probable dehydration diagnosis and an Urgent priority. The page lists these as the cluster that together makes dehydration likely (it uses explicit 'or' elsewhere on the same line-set when it means any-of, e.g. 'Difficulty breathing or respiratory rate >= 30', and explicit 'and' in the heart-failure item). The honest reading is a conjunction or at least any2; 'or' over-triggers both the diagnosis and the Urgent level.
evidence: Diagnose probable dehydration (weakness or tiredness page) :: (or (clinical_finding (snomed_concept "Increased thirst" "finding")) (clinical_finding (snomed_concept "Xerostomia" "finding")) (clinical_finding (snomed_concept "Decreased skin turgor" "finding")) (< (measurement (snomed_concept "Systolic blood pressure" "observable entity") mmHg) 90) (< (measurement (snomed_concept "Diastolic blood pressure" "observable entity") mmHg) 60))
Urgent: weakness or tiredness with red-box findings :: (active_condition (snomed_concept "Dehydration" "disorder"))

rule_level_problems.rule: Diagnose probable dehydration (weakness or tiredness page)
rule_level_problems.problem: 'or' across thirst / dry mouth / poor skin turgor / BP < 90/60 where the page lists them as a cluster. Any single soft sign (thirst) in a tired patient produces a probable Dehydration diagnosis, which the priority rule then promotes to Urgent via (active_condition Dehydration). The page does not justify Urgent for thirst alone. An 'and', or an any2 with BP as its own group, would match the page's intent.

rule_level_problems.rule: Urgent: weakness or tiredness with red-box findings
rule_level_problems.problem: (active_condition Fever) has no onset bound although the page limits it to the past 3 days and the language has onset / time_ago comparisons. Any historical fever record makes the patient Urgent.

rule_level_problems.rule: Diagnose probable heart failure / probable dehydration (weakness or tiredness page)
rule_level_problems.problem: Both probable rules use (clinical_finding Asthenia) as evidence. Fatigue is a common symptom, but Asthenia is not on the common-symptom list and appears in this file only inside the check task's (or ...) due_to, never as a check_for item. If the test's 'checked for in the same file' match is by exact s-expression of the leaf, this may be flagged. Cannot verify without the VHA test; noting only.

summary: The red box is encoded almost completely and with the right concepts: stroke/TIA findings, glucose thresholds, chest pain, difficulty breathing / RR >= 30, heart failure (orthopnea and leg swelling, probable), worsening leg weakness and temperature >= 38 are all correct, and Hb < 6 is correctly left out as not representable. The one substantive error is the dehydration rule, which uses 'or' over thirst, dry mouth, poor skin turgor and BP < 90/60, so thirst alone yields a probable dehydration diagnosis and an Urgent priority the page does not justify. A minor gap: 'fever in the past 3 days' is encoded as an unbounded active Fever condition although the language can express the 3-day window.
